transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Alvarez (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Evan Moore (Cassiopeia CTO), Sana Park (Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (SRE), Marta Ruiz (PM)
Links: perf spreadsheet (to be shared), shared bucket (Cassiopeia)

Summary (auto): quick read of lab numbers, triage on throughput delta, agree on rerun and canary window

00:00 Jordan Alvarez: hey everyone thanks for taking time, quick roll call?
00:05 Evan Moore: Evan here, yup
00:07 Sana Park: Sana on, sorry bit of background noise
00:10 Jordan Alvarez: great, Jordan and Priya from Redwood. today we want to walk the bench deltas vs your incumbent and line up the reruns you asked for last week
00:19 Priya Raman: yeah we'll go through the spreadsheet, call out where KV priming and batching interplayed, and propose a quantized run for the long-context cases
00:28 Marta Ruiz: quick ask — can you flag anything that needs product signoff? we have a compliance window coming up end of month

02:12 Jordan Alvarez: ok jumping to slide one of the perf sheet - short prompts, <64 tokens, median p50 latency is basically parity with IncumbentAI; p95 is slightly better on Redwood in hosted config, about 30-40ms improvement
02:34 Sana Park: when you say hosted config, is that your multi-tenant hosted or dedicated reserved slots?
02:38 Jordan Alvarez: this was on hosted API with adaptive batching and prefix KV cache enabled; dedicated shows a tighter tail once we pin weights and isolate GPUs
02:55 Evan Moore: can you remind us about the KV cache priming approach? last run I remember numbers moving a lot after warmup
03:05 Priya Raman: sure. priming is essentially preloading the KV cache with recent tokens for the common prompt prefixes — that reduces repeated attention recompute. warmup matters, and for your workload (lots of repeated templates) priming knocked down per-token compute by ~10-15% in our lab run
03:27 Liam O'Connor: that 10-15% was seen in throughput or just CPU/GPU usage?
03:33 Priya Raman: mostly throughput; because lower compute per token means more requests per GPU concurrently before hitting thermal or batch size limits
03:48 Jordan Alvarez: side note — transcription might say K-V cash, we've seen that before — it's KV cache, not cash, sorry for the bad joke

06:02 Jordan Alvarez: mid-run sustained throughput checks: we ran a 30 minute ramp to 200 RPS; Redwood sustained about 18% higher qps compared to IncumbentAI at equivalent 99ms p95 target when batching aggressively
06:23 Sana Park: 18% is promising — what's the tokenization differences? could our pretokenization be giving you an edge?
06:30 Priya Raman: good question. we normalized on the same tokenizer and token counts for both vendors; but the incumbent had smaller batch sizes by default in their infra which limited packing efficiency
06:46 Evan Moore: so it's more packing and batching efficiency than raw model compute difference?
06:50 Priya Raman: mostly, yes. also our kernel selection and fusion for the attention kernels gives a small per-token win, but the biggest wins came from continuous batching and KV reuse
07:13 Marta Ruiz: what about quantized runs? we heard LocalQuantEdge had strong unit-cost but worse latency — curious how Redwood fairs
07:22 Priya Raman: we did an int8-quantized pass in the lab. single-request tail latency rose a bit for long contexts but throughput improved significantly under load. tradeoff depends on SLOs — if p95 < 150ms strict, we recommend mixed strategy: quantized for background heavy workloads and float for low-latency critical flows
07:51 Liam O'Connor: can Redwood fall back automatically to float if quantized misses the tail?
07:56 Jordan Alvarez: yes with Dedicated you can configure routing policies; Redwood Optimize can auto-fallback to float model variants on latency SLO violations — that's something we can show in the canary

10:02 Evan Moore: security — we need to sync SOC2 timing and SSO. our security team will want to see audit logs and KMS flow. where are you on SOC2?
10:12 Jordan Alvarez: Redwood is SOC2 Type II certified; we provide audit logs, SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM for key separation
10:25 Sana Park: any gotchas for VPC peering? Liam will need to whitelist IPs and we want to do a short connectivity test during the canary window
10:33 Liam O'Connor: yes I'll need the IP ranges. also need to confirm whether the VP C peering supports egress NAT for your control plane calls
10:40 Jordan Alvarez: we'll share the IP list and a step-by-step VPC peering checklist in the perf spreadsheet bundle

13:15 Priya Raman: back to numbers — here's the matrix we care about: short prompts p95, long prompts p95, sustained throughput at 100/200/500 RPS, and unit token cost. Redwood beat incumbent on unit cost by ~9% in our runs after tuning batching and cache; however for extreme long contexts (>2048) incumbent's model variant had slight tail advantages in some samples
13:42 Sana Park: that's interesting — which model variants did you test for the long context?
13:46 Priya Raman: we tested Redwood-XL-compat (float32) and a Redwood-XL-quant (int8), and matched them to the incumbent's long-context offering. the incumbent used their custom long-context config; we saw variance on worst-case dokooms — uh — docooms — document cases
14:05 Jordan Alvarez: oops transcription note: docooms -> document examples, meaning long single doc prompts

16:00 Marta Ruiz: timeline — we have a compliance freeze 02/28. to hit it we need pilot decision by 02/20. Is that feasible?
16:12 Evan Moore: product wants canary before decision so we can validate production telemetry and audit logs
16:18 Jordan Alvarez: feasible. proposed plan: quantized rerun with KV priming and long-context sample set (this week), then dedicated canary week of 02/15 for 48 hours with ramp to steady qps. we should have telemetry and logs for your security and product teams before 02/20 decision
16:36 Sana Park: internal ML team wants to run a 1k prompt representative set — we'll push that by Monday if possible

20:20 Priya Raman: small technical note — we need to align on the prompt distribution. your dataset has a lot of repetition and templated fields which plays well with KV reuse. if you have more diverse prompts the throughput delta will narrow
20:40 Evan Moore: good to know. we'll flag a high-diversity subset as well so you can test worst-case scenarios

23:00 Liam O'Connor: operational question — on incidents does Redwood expose traces with per-request token-level timing? we want that for SRE dashboards
23:08 Jordan Alvarez: yes we expose per-request traces and token-level timing; you can forward to your observability stack or use our Console for trace drilldowns. export hooks via tracing API and we also provide per-route latency breakdowns

26:55 Priya Raman: troubleshooting notes from last run: we saw a small increase in p95 at 10k concurrent tokens due to KV eviction thresholds — we tweaked cache retention and saw normalization. we'll include the exact config lines in the results bundle
27:18 Sana Park: can we get the exact autobalance and batch timeout settings? those are sensitive for us because we tie into downstream SLA calculations
27:26 Priya Raman: absolutely. default batch timeout we used was 12ms for high throughput runs; we can test 8/12/20ms for sensitivity. autobalance is adaptive based on observed queueing, we'll share the heuristic doc

30:05 Jordan Alvarez: quick note on pricing delta — unit token cost after tuning was about 9% lower than incumbent; with dedicated reserved slots that margin improves further but requires commit. we ran a committed projection in the sheet showing 15-22% savings at your expected monthly volume
30:27 Evan Moore: that's compelling. product/finance will want a worked example with our traffic profile and weekly burst patterns
30:36 Jordan Alvarez: we'll tailor that in the spreadsheet, will include worst-case and optimistic usage curves

33:40 Marta Ruiz: questions from legal — do you have standard terms for data residency and retention? Cassiopeia needs 7 year audit trail for certain logs
33:52 Jordan Alvarez: we support configurable retention policies and long-term audit exports. for Private deployments you can own the audit store. for hosted we'll propose an archive flow to your S3 with encryption via your KMS
34:05 Sana Park: small point — earlier we noticed a mis-annotation in one run where function-calling tokens were counted differently between vendors; could that skew cost numbers?
34:16 Priya Raman: yes function call overhead sometimes gets double-counted depending on how the bench harness measures request vs generated tokens. we'll normalize on your harness definitions in the rerun

36:10 Evan Moore: any outstanding blockers to run the quantized group this week?
36:17 Priya Raman: we need the 1k prompt set and permission to run the dedicated canary; also access to your shared bucket for uploading results would speed iteration
36:26 Jordan Alvarez: action items we'll capture — Jordan to push spreadsheet and IP list; Priya to schedule rerun and run quantized test; Evan/Sana to share prompt set and confirm canary window

40:02 Marta Ruiz: last question — how would an automatic fallback look in practice? we want zero visible errors for end users if quantized misses an SLO
40:12 Jordan Alvarez: Redwood's routing policy can check p50/p95 and automatically re-route to float variant when observed tail breaches SLO threshold for N consecutive requests. it's configurable and we can demo it in the canary

44:00 Jordan Alvarez: recap and next steps — Jordan will share perf spreadsheet + IP list by 02/07; Priya will run quantized rerun with KV priming and share results by 02/09; Cassiopeia to upload 1k representative prompts by 02/08; schedule canary on dedicated pool week of 02/15; we'll have a check-in after the rerun to confirm canary timing

46:20 Evan Moore: thanks all, this was useful.
46:25 Sana Park: thanks
46:27 Jordan Alvarez: thanks everyone, we will follow up with the bundle and notes
46:33 (call end)
notes: Perf spreadsheet link (to be shared), VPC peering checklist, quantized config defaults included in follow-up. Rerun to normalize token counting for function calls.
